summary: CKPRST is a callable Checkpoint/Restart service, intended to manage checkpoints against an indexed checkpoint file so long-running batch jobs can be restarted after a failure. It is invoked with a checkpoint-control area and a return-status area, and dispatches on an entry-point code to one of four operations: INIT, TAKE (take a checkpoint), COMMIT, or RESTART. IMPORTANT: this program is currently an UNIMPLEMENTED SKELETON — the four operation paragraphs contain only comments and no executable statements, so no checkpoint logic actually runs yet.

paragraphs.name: MAINLINE
paragraphs.pseudocode:
SELECT CASE entry point (from CHECKPOINT-CONTROL)
  WHEN INIT:    CALL PROC-INIT
  WHEN TAKE:    CALL PROC-TAKE-CHECKPOINT
  WHEN COMMIT:  CALL PROC-COMMIT-CHECKPOINT
  WHEN RESTART: CALL PROC-RESTART
END SELECT
RETURN to caller (GOBACK)

annotations.note: Called as a sub-routine (PROCEDURE DIVISION USING CHECKPOINT-CONTROL RETURN-STATUS).
EVALUATE has no WHEN OTHER — an unrecognised entry point silently does nothing and returns.
